business.what_it_does: Scribe automatically captures how work gets done — turning actions taken in web, mobile and desktop apps into step-by-step how-to guides, documentation, training material, and context for AI agents.

facts.statement: Upgrading a team to a Pro plan upgrades the whole team unless a separate team is created for just the members needing Pro.

provenance.quote: If I upgrade to a Pro plan, does my whole team get upgraded as well? Yes. If you have a team on Scribe, when you upgrade to Pro it will also upgrade your teammates. dossier.orientation: Scribe is documentation software that records the steps of a procedure performed in an application and turns them into a step-by-step how-to guide for an IT team to share.

setup_conditions: Use Scribe in the browser on the free Basic plan to generate how-to guides (E1)
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires a Pro or Enterprise account (E5)
All members of one Scribe team must sit on the same plan tier, and upgrading a team upgrades every member unless a separate team is created (E7, E6)
decision_gaps: Does Scribe's documentation state that each captured step includes a screenshot, and on which plans?
Does Scribe document a mechanism for updating an existing guide when the underlying system or UI changes?

unverified_requirement_basis.Reuse of the captured procedures as stru: "reused as training or as structured context for internal AI tools"

defining_need_fit.caveat: The selected evidence establishes automatic capture of already-performed work into guides (E12) and browser-based guide generation on the free tier (E1), but screenshot output, update-on-change behaviour and AI-context reuse are not established by the selected evidence; team-wide rollout also carries same-tier and whole-team upgrade conditions (E7, E6).
defining_need_fit.why: Only the capture-and-generate component of the stated need is supported by cited evidence, so the conjunction with currency and AI-context reuse remains partial.

first_email_scope.request: Write exactly one email. Introduce our product to a new buyer with one clear next step.
first_email_scope.workflow: On the free Basic plan the buyer can create an account and, in their browser, manually walk through one IT procedure they currently only hold in their head (for example a browser-based software setup or account configuration) and have Scribe generate it as a how-to guide they can share.
setup_conditions: Free Basic account; guide generation happens in the browser by manually performing the steps (E1)
Procedure must be performed in a web application, since desktop capture is a Pro or Enterprise feature (E5)
excluded_promises: No claim that the team can scale documentation organisation-wide without a paid plan
No claim of zero disruption to current ticket or wiki practice
No claim of avoided or reduced headcount
No claim of replacing or outperforming an incumbent documentation tool
No claim that guides stay current automatically or feed internal AI tools
No time-saved or error-reduction promise applied to this buyer
No claim that Autocapture (turning already-completed work into Scribes automatically) is available on the Basic plan — the evidence for this feature does not specify which plan tier includes it
No claim that sensitive data redaction (PII/PHI) applies to Basic-plan guide generation — that protection is evidenced only for Enterprise or unspecified-plan contexts

ranked_relevance.why: States the core mechanism: work already performed is turned into Scribes automatically, which is exactly the undocumented-procedure task.
The free Basic plan generating how-to guides in the browser is the only next step whose entitlement is documented without a purchase.
Names the plan boundary of desktop capture, which bounds any claim about documenting non-browser IT procedures.
Pro Team pricing with its 5-seat minimum and annual-billing condition is the documented path once documentation moves beyond one person.
Automatic redaction of 150 categories of PII, PHI and PCI is the documented answer to capturing screens inside internal IT systems.
SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, FERPA and GDPR compliance plus fine-grained workspace permissions are the documented facts a mid-size to large IT function will be asked about.
The AI-agent performance figure is an unattributed Pro Team and Enterprise survey stat and would overstate the unverified AI-context part of this need.
Same-tier-only teams explain internally why a team rollout is a single tier decision, but it is not a claim to put to a first-contact buyer.

problem_fits.caveat: The problem rests on a single 2019 forum source whose present applicability is uncorroborated, and capture of desktop-app procedures requires Pro or Enterprise (E5).
problem_fits.why: Autocapture turning already-performed work into guides is a documented mechanism for converting undocumented tribal knowledge into written procedure.

segment_objections.objection: Much of our IT work happens in desktop applications and consoles, not a browser, so a browser capture tool would miss it.
segment_objections.answer: Desktop capture exists but is a Pro and Enterprise feature, not part of the free Basic account.

segment_objections.objection: Capturing our IT procedures means recording screens containing user and system data we cannot let leave our control.
segment_objections.answer: Scribe states that 150 categories of PII, PHI and PCI are redacted automatically and that it is SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, FERPA and GDPR compliant with fine-grained workspace permissions.
